title: Quantum-Geometric Length Scale for Long-distance Squeezing in Bosonic Bogoliubov Systems
authors: Sonu Verma, Sangmo Cheon, Myung-Joong Hwang, Moon Jip Park
abstract: Multimode squeezing is a key resource for continuous-variable quantum technologies, but its spatial range in bosonic lattices is usually tied to dispersive propagation. Here we show that parametric pairing can create an exactly flat Bogoliubov band spanned by compact Bogoliubov generators, while producing phase-sensitive anomalous correlations and sub-vacuum collective-mode squeezing that extend far beyond their finite support. Each compact generator mixes annihilation and creation operators, thereby encoding the Bogoliubov squeezing structure, and neighboring translated generators can have nonzero commutator overlap. Enforcing canonical bosonic commutation relations therefore requires spatially extended linear combinations of these translated compact generators, which define the canonical Bogoliubov modes. The squeezing transformation of these modes varies with momentum and is quantified by the squeezing-sector symplectic quantum metric. A complex-momentum singularity of the analytically continued canonical Bogoliubov modes sets both the anomalous-correlation decay length and the momentum-space width of this metric, defining an intrinsic quantum-geometric length scale. This singularity can be tuned continuously while preserving exact flatness, thereby controlling the spatial range of correlations and squeezing. Away from exact flatness, long-distance correlations persist through multiple decay channels, while modes localized by defects and dimerized boundaries provide complementary probes of the underlying quantum geometry. In the weak-damping limit, the same quantum-geometric length scale can be extracted from frequency-filtered two-port correlations. Our results establish the quantum geometry of canonical Bogoliubov modes as a mechanism for spatially extended quantum resources arising from compact Bogoliubov generators.
summary: The authors demonstrate that engineered flat bands in bosonic lattices enable long-range quantum correlations and squeezing, bypassing limitations imposed by dispersive wave propagation. They introduce an intrinsic quantum-geometric length scale ($\xi_S$), determined by a complex-momentum singularity, which governs the decay of these non-classical resources. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for controlling quantum resources in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses how to achieve and quantify long-distance, phase-sensitive quantum correlations and sub-vacuum squeezing in bosonic lattices without relying on standard dispersive propagation mechanisms.
main_result: Parametric pairing can create an exactly flat Bogoliubov band, defining an intrinsic quantum-geometric length scale ($\xi_S$) that controls the spatial range of squeezing and anomalous correlations.
method: The analysis involves constructing canonical Bogoliubov modes from compact generators and quantifying squeezing using the squeezing-sector symplectic quantum metric, linking the scale to a complex-momentum singularity.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional bosonic lattice modeled using Bogoliubov theory, specifically utilizing parametric pairing ($\Delta(k)$) to engineer an exactly flat band ($\omega_f$) within the spectrum.
key_observables: Anomalous correlation $F(R)$, sub-vacuum squeezing depth $D_{	ext{out}}(R)$, and the intrinsic quantum-geometric length scale $\xi_S$.
important_parameters: The flat band frequency ($\omega_f$), the complex-momentum singularity location ($z_S$), and the weak-damping limit.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of an exactly flat band and, in some analyses, assumes the weak-linewidth and narrow-filter limit for pole structure analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the lattice setup showing the flat band, the mechanism involving compact generators, and the relationship between the correlation decay length and the momentum-space width defined by $\xi_S$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical model (flat band via pairing) to deriving the mathematical structure (canonical modes, symplectic metric) and finally quantifying the resulting physical resource (squeezing range and length scale $\xi_S$) through various diagnostic tools.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical link between the spectral geometry (flat bands) of interacting bosonic systems and the spatial extent of non-classical quantum resources like squeezing, which is highly relevant for quantum simulation and quantum optics.
